Allwinner A64 PCB Layout Guide V1.0 pp20–21 requires the two shared clock/address branch lengths to differ by less than 50 mil. Assessment compares U2 and U3 paths of each shared net, so their common trunk cancels. This is not a within-byte tolerance.

ST AN5122 package + via + PCB constraints are assessed separately using the AA/LFBGA448 workbook and complete series-clock paths. The original board supplies total thickness but no inner-layer stackup, so via depth is bounded rather than guessed: https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/dm00462392-stm32mp1-series-ddr-memory-routing-guidelines-stmicroelectronics.pdf
Legacy class DDR_CLK_LM1.0 has no assigned retained nets; no target is created for an empty class.

ECP5 guide §9 checks trace matching against both strobe/clock conductors. Relative and overlapping inter-group requirements are assessed only; Core has no equivalent reference-net tuning option. Via-count/stackup and non-skew hardware requirements are outside these planar checks.

Use WP479's newer DDR3 endpoint-delay requirements for DQ/DM and address/control, replacing the older UG388 planar equivalents. WP479 p3/p11 explicitly removes DQS-to-CK and inter-byte DQS matching; neither is imposed. Retain UG388's 10 mil P/N PCB pair guidance, with WP479's additional 2 ps DQS-pair checks. Delay assessment uses the original stackup and bounded FPGA package skew; it is an estimate, not SI signoff.

notes: NXP IMX6ULLHDG Rev 0 Table 21 byte-group strategy: 2 inch clock maximum; 5 mil CK pair, 10 mil DQS pair, 25 mil byte/address and 50 mil control matching. Use a conservative full-spread interpretation of the ± matching figures. Address/control must be 0–200 mil shorter than the shortest CK; bytes must not exceed it. The alternative all-signals-to-clock strategy is not combined with this one.
